kpis.label: Operating margin
kpis.note: GAAP, up from 5.0% a year ago

oneTimers: Restructuring charges of $8M — down from $711M a year ago — sit inside operating expenses.

A $37M gain on strategic investments, net — a swing from a $141M loss a year ago. Per the 10-Q it was primarily $105M of unrealized gains on privately held stakes and $59M of realized gains on sales, partly offset by $130M of impairments.
otherDetail: A $37M gain on strategic investments (stakes Salesforce holds in other companies), plus $121M of other income — mostly interest earned, net of interest on Salesforce's debt: a net $158M.

takeaways.text: GAAP operating margin reached 18.7%, up from 5.0% a year ago, as operating income rose to $1.71B from $412M. The big swing was restructuring: $8M of charges this quarter versus $711M a year ago.
takeaways.title: Margins jumped as restructuring faded

takeaways.text: Second-quarter revenue guidance of $9.20B to $9.25B implies growth of just 7% to 8%, and Salesforce lowered its full-year subscription and support growth guidance to slightly below 10% while holding total revenue guidance at $37.7B to $38.0B.
takeaways.title: Next quarter guided slower

takeaways.text: Current remaining performance obligation — work customers have signed for and will pay for within a year — rose 10% to $26.4B. Operating cash flow rose 39% to $6.25B, and Salesforce returned $2.2B through share repurchases plus $0.4B in its first-ever quarterly dividend.
takeaways.title: Backlog up, cash returned

verdict: Salesforce grew revenue 11% to $9.13B, expanded GAAP operating margin to 18.7% from 5.0% a year ago as restructuring charges fell from $711M to $8M, and lifted net income to $1.53B from $199M while returning $2.2B through buybacks and paying its first-ever dividend.
